interpretation: Under the Paper 11 convention Delta_mu = -kappa X, the canonical nested clock-rate prediction has the established massive-host-brighter sign and literature-step order (~0.04-0.05 mag), but it overshoots the post-correction residual in this m_b_corr mini-analysis. The frozen kappa_SN = kappa_Cep-equiv = 3.69e5 mag is a cross-channel transfer, while the data-implied kappa_SN on this corrected product is reported separately and is opposite signed — a two-point binary-step estimate on the released vector, which is unpinned (residual step +0.006 mag is consistent with zero). The correctly posed continuous-X generalized-least-squares fit on the raw standardization columns (scripts/steps/audit_env_response_kappa.py, results/outputs/audit_env_response_kappa.json) instead returns kappa_SN = +3.2e4 +/- 1.1e4 mag (2.9 sigma, predicted deep-well-brighter direction), replicated on DES-Dovekie at +8.9e4 +/- 2.3e4 (3.9 sigma). The binary implied-kappa below is retained as a diagnostic record; the continuous-coordinate GLS estimate is the authoritative SN-channel measurement. The raw conformal clock ratio contributes only ~5e-7 mag, so the step is carried by the response sector, consistent with the Paper 0 amplitude/screening split. This step is therefore a channel-consistency diagnostic, not an independent confirmation of the host-mass correction.
